gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now runs the gpio_wdt, bcm2835_wdt, and dw_wdt starter tests together with the dedicated dw_wdt suspend-resume replay, the dedicated remove-idle split replay, and the dw_wdt survey gate so the simple-driver watchdog tranche stays reviewable in one place.

A dedicated survey gate now records that the dw_wdt starter, probe summary, dedicated tests, remove-handoff teardown evidence, and validation-matrix status already exist while keeping the remaining registration-facing and platform-facing gaps explicit instead of letting the current scaffold overclaim parity.

The survey note now anchors the live dw_wdt lane to `master` `907e65f13e0035306d4106dec0ca3b3eb2fc7179` so later runs can extend the same Phase 11 slice without rediscovering the landed platform-resource preflight packet, remove-handoff teardown evidence, validation-matrix evidence, or the current review packet provenance.

The bounded starter already derives fixed TOP timeout windows, mirrors reset-mode versus IRQ-mode timeout selection and pretimeout bookkeeping, and now exposes both a probe-time summary and a registration-facing handoff alongside register-image transitions, plus a bounded `summarizeRemoveHandoff()` packet for the unconditional debugfs clear call site, unregister-device ordering, and reset-control-backed versus non-reset remove fallout without claiming live debugfs support or platform-backed behavior.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep fixed-top limits, custom-top ordering, probe-time bookkeeping, registration-facing watchdog info and parent handoff details, platform-resource preflight and live resource-order sequencing, reset-mode and IRQ-mode timeout behavior, restart intent, non-stoppable stop semantics, remove-handoff teardown parity, and the debugfs-clear call-site ownership boundary reviewable around the landed starter.

The lane now records that include/uapi/linux/watchdog.h still owns struct watchdog_info plus the WDIOC_* and WDIOF_* or WDIOS_* surface, while include/linux/watchdog.h still owns watchdog_device and watchdog_ops so the DesignWare slice does not overclaim public-header or watchdog-core parity.

The slice note now records the exact starter contract, including the bounded remove-handoff teardown packet and its debugfs-clear ownership boundary, so the repo does not blur the current in-memory driver model into clock, reset, IRQ, debugfs, or hardware-backed parity.

A dedicated validation matrix now centralizes the shared Phase 11 test gate, fixed-TOP timeout evidence, IRQ pretimeout bookkeeping, imported running-state handoff evidence, bounded suspend-resume state-preservation evidence, non-stoppable stop failure-mode coverage, the landed remove-handoff teardown parity, the debugfs-clear call-site boundary, the landed platform-resource preflight plus live resource-order summary, and the exact replay commands so the DesignWare lane does not overclaim platform-driver or PM parity.

The starter now includes a tiny probe-time summary around fixed-versus-custom TOP sourcing, nowayout and restart-priority bookkeeping, stop-on-reboot intent, and already-running watchdog state before any platform-backed behavior lands.

The starter now includes a small registration-facing handoff that keeps watchdog info selection, parent linkage, driver-data setup, timeout-init intent, imported running-state bookkeeping, and register-device intent explicit before any live clock, reset, IRQ, or MMIO work.

The starter now includes a tiny platform-resource preflight plus live resource-order summary around timer-clock choice, optional APB clock presence, reset-control availability, optional pretimeout-IRQ wiring, and the bounded tclk, optional pclk, reset, irq, and registration sequencing before any live devm calls or watchdog registration work lands.

Platform-driver registration, live clock and reset acquisition, IRQ registration, suspend and resume handling, debugfs support, devicetree TOP arrays, and live MMIO validation remain blocked until the lane grows beyond the landed registration handoff, remove-handoff teardown packet, and platform-resource preflight into a hardware-validation plan.
